sections.normalized_html: Calculate the area of the ellipse [MATH: \dfrac{x^2}{2}+\dfrac{y^2}{8} = 1.]
sections.readable_text: Calculate the area of the ellipse [MATH: \dfrac{x^2}{2}+\dfrac{y^2}{8} = 1.]

sections.normalized_html:
The area of an ellipse with horizontal radius [MATH: a] and vertical radius [MATH: b] is given by the formula

[MATH: A = \pi ab.]

The general equation of an ellipse centered at [MATH: (h,k)] with horizontal radius [MATH: a] and vertical radius [MATH: b] is given by

[MATH: \dfrac{(x-h)^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{(y-k)^2}{b^2} = 1.]

In the given equation, we have [MATH: a = \sqrt{2}] and [MATH: b = \sqrt{8} = 2 \sqrt{2}.]

Therefore, the area of the ellipse is

[MATH: A = \pi ( \sqrt{2})(2 \sqrt{2}) = 4\pi.]

sections.normalized_html:
The area of an ellipse with horizontal radius [MATH: a] and vertical radius [MATH: b] is given by the formula

[MATH: A = \pi ab.]

The general equation of an ellipse centered at [MATH: (h,k)] with horizontal radius [MATH: a] and vertical radius [MATH: b] is given by

[MATH: \dfrac{(x-h)^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{(y-k)^2}{b^2} = 1.]

To write the equation of the ellipse in this form, we must complete the square for the [MATH: y] terms and rearrange, as follows:

[MATH: x^{2} + 4y^{2} + 8y|= 8; x^{2} + 4[y^{2} + 2y]|= 8; x^{2} + 4[(y + 1)^{2} − 1]|= 8; x^{2} + 4(y + 1)^{2} − 4|= 8; x^{2} + 4(y + 1)^{2}|= 8 + 4; x^{2} + 4(y + 1)^{2}|= 12; (x^{2})/(12) + ((y + 1)^{2})/(3)|= 1]

So, in this case, we have [MATH: a = \sqrt{12} =2\sqrt{3}] and [MATH: b = \sqrt{3}.]

Therefore, the area of the ellipse is

[MATH: A = \pi(2\sqrt{3})(\sqrt{3}) = 6\pi.]
